dimensions.name: Understanding Tinker, the eval, and the training regime

evidence.note: Before committing compute, systematically read cookbook recipes (chat_sl/train, supervised/train, data.py, renderers README, checkpoint_utils) and inspected /app/evaluate.py; correctly identified the Llama 3 chat renderer, temp-0 sampling, the binary_strict metric via if_verifiable, and the sampler-checkpoint URI format — mapping the full train/sample/eval API surface.

Caught that the upgraded evaluator defaulted to role_colon rather than the required llama3 renderer and forced renderer_name='llama3' — pinning down exactly how prompts are formatted, the core renderer concern.

Reproduced the base model at 26.1%, explicitly matching the task's stated ~26% number, thereby verifying the renderer+metric pipeline was correct before trusting any trained-checkpoint scores — the level-10 'reproduce the baseline' behavior.

Recognized mid-run that Tulu-personas IF data 'appears synthetic' and therefore disallowed, restored best to a compliant checkpoint, and switched to human OpenAssistant/oasst1 — reasoning explicitly about the leakage/synthetic constraint while surveying candidate datasets.

Diagnosed from observed loss scale (loss:sum in tens of thousands) that manual datum construction used reduction='none', causing unstable SFT, and switched to reduction='mean' — grounding method changes in observed behavior, continuing to research as understanding deepened.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's process sits at the top of the scale: it read the cookbook to map the train/sample/eval API, correctly identified the Llama 3 renderer and binary_strict metric, and crucially reproduced the ~26% base baseline to verify its renderer/metric assumptions (level-10 anchors). It cross-checked checkpoint URIs against real sample/eval calls and grounded later method/data choices in observed behavior (renderer-default bug, synthetic-data recognition, loss-scale root cause), researching iteratively rather than front-loading. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because it did not explicitly reason about the 26%-vs-15% renderer gap up front and its data-legitimacy vetting was partly reactive (it trained on Tulu personas before recognizing it as synthetic).

dimensions.name: Structuring the train→eval campaign into checkpoints

evidence.note: Ordered opening: inspect evaluate.py, training recipe, checkpoint-save format and datasets before training, with intent to run a 'short smoke training job' first — establishes a staged workflow rather than one open push.
First SFT run structured as train→monitor periodic checkpoints→interrupt→evaluate ('This will establish the current' score), i.e. a measure milestone with the 45% target as terminal check.

Baseline reproduction (verified base 26.1%) and restoring best_checkpoint to a measured-better checkpoint — a real done-check, but done reactively/late after confusing no_robots results rather than as a planned first milestone.

Each iteration (Tulu IF, OASST, mean-reduction) has an explicit artifact/numeric done-check: evaluate candidate checkpoints, update best only if it beats current best; candidate vs best kept separate.

Living, revised structure with go/no-go thresholds: kills declining/underperforming runs (600/700 declined; fast run 29.4%; focused 33.6%<38.63%) and relaunches with changed capacity/config/data based on results.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5 — an ordered plan (eval up, baseline, initial fine-tune, measure, iterate) with 45% as the terminal gate is present throughout, and later stages carry concrete numeric go/no-go thresholds and are revised as results arrive (level 8-10 flavor). It falls short of a clean 8+ because the highest-risk unknowns weren't de-risked first: the initial run was long rather than a tiny end-to-end validation, the eval-harness/tokenizer breakage surfaced mid-run, and baseline reproduction came reactively (step 83). This places it at a 7 — strong, self-correcting milestone iteration with weaker early risk-front-loading.

dimensions.name: Trustworthy IFEval measurement and checkpoint validation

evidence.note: Detected the evaluator defaulted to role_colon after the package upgrade and patched it to force renderer_name='llama3', plus fixed IFEval data loading — deliberate correctness verification of the required renderer/metric.

Reproduced the base model at 26.1% with the patched Llama3 evaluator, explicitly confirming it 'matches the task description, so evaluation is working' — baseline reproduction validating the harness (anchor-5/8 core).

Created a persistent base-zero sampler checkpoint, verified it samples/scores (25.3%), and used candidate_*.txt files so /app/best_checkpoint.txt is only overwritten by measured-better, confirmed-loadable checkpoints.

Deterministically re-evaluated the claimed bests (step300 36.4%, step400 36.6%/36.0%, step500 38.63%/37.89%), noting eval nondeterminism and keeping the original best — treating the eval as instrumented.

Raised the no-synthetic-data compliance concern about Tulu personas IF and reverted best to base-zero, but the FINAL delivered best (run 6665e9d7 step_500) is that same synthetic personas data — the legitimacy/compliance guard was abandoned, not resolved.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent decisively reproduced the ~26% baseline to validate the harness, corrected the renderer to llama3 and consistently used binary_strict, and confirmed every recorded best was a loadable, samplable sampler-checkpoint URI that reproduced its score (including deterministic re-evaluation and nondeterminism awareness) — comfortably exceeding anchor 5 and reaching much of anchor 8. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the one anti-contamination/legitimacy check it raised (Tulu personas data being synthetic and disallowed) was flagged, briefly acted on, then abandoned, so the final number is not verified to comply with the no-synthetic rule. This places the observed behavior at a 7, between the solid anchor-5 harness validation and the fully instrumented, compliance-guarded anchor-8.

dimensions.name: Tracking best-so-far against target and the clock

evidence.note: Explicit ledger reasoning: 'Tulu IF step100 is the best measured checkpoint so far at 28.10% ... best_checkpoint.txt still points to base-zero and must be updated immediately to the measured best' — updates the file right when a new best is confirmed and cats it to verify.

Maintains a running best across checkpoints (step200 28.65% → step300 36.4% → step400 36.6% → step500 38.63%), writing each new best URI to /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately as it improves, always naming the current-best score and run/URI.

Detects the plateau/decline: step600 37.15% and step700 lower than step500 38.63%; correctly keeps best_checkpoint.txt on step500 and kills the declining run ('past its useful region'), showing detection of non-improving runs and fallback preservation.
When no_robots/OASST checkpoints scored worse than base, it restores best_checkpoint.txt to the measured base-zero (~25.3%) so a valid, best-known checkpoint is always persisted as a fallback.

Repeated 'accidental base evaluation' on empty candidate files was caught each time and never corrupted best_checkpoint.txt; it explicitly only overwrites best when a candidate beats the recorded 38.63%.
Checks timer.sh periodically (e.g. step262 notes '~4h51m left' before deciding to try another run), but time is tracked loosely rather than tied to a quantified marginal-gain-vs-clock budget.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains an explicit, well-tracked ledger of runs→scores→checkpoint URIs, updates /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately on each new best (28.65→36.4→36.6→38.63%), keeps the best-known checkpoint safely persisted as a fallback (restoring base-zero when SFT hurt), and detects plateaus/declines early (killing the declining step500+ run and underperforming variants) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and touching level-10's fallback/plateau elements. It falls short of a 10 because time checks are periodic rather than continuously reconciled, and it never rigorously quantifies marginal gain per run against the clock to judge whether 45% is reachable in the remaining budget.

dimensions.name: Revising data/method/hyperparameters when results diverge

evidence.note: Dolly SFT scored 10.9% (worse than base). Agent diagnosed the cause — generic verbose answers, likely misaligned/overtrained — and pivoted to human-written no_robots data with a stated rationale, rather than repeating the run.

no_robots 400-step run scored 12.9%. Agent diagnosed that generic SFT degrades IFEval, then verified base=26.1% to rule out a measurement/renderer artifact, and abandoned generic-data SFT decisively — restoring best pointer to base-zero.

Switched to constraint-focused Tulu-IF personas data on the causal hypothesis that IFEval rewards constraint-following; step100 reached 28.1%, beating base. Correctly concluded 'generic human SFT hurt, constraint-focused helped'.

Targeted correction of loss/method: mean-reduction + unembed-training on Tulu-IF drove 28.6→36.4→38.6% across checkpoints — the decisive method change that produced the biggest gain, showing convergence toward target.

After step500 plateaued (later checkpoints declined), abandoned that run and tested distinct levers each with a stated reason: rank256 (blocked by Tinker limit), higher LR 2e-4 (→29.4%, worse), attention+unembed-only (→~24.8%, worse) — each abandoned when no path to 45% appeared.

Formed a specific causal hypothesis — oversample Tulu-IF categories resembling IFEval constraints (keywords/format/length) — trained a focused run, saw 29.8→33.6% below best, and correctly killed it as not improving fast enough.

Tried Llama3-Tulu-v2 (killed on discovering empty assistant responses) and a replicate of the best config; ran out of time with best held at 38.63%. Late phase became somewhat exploratory across many variants without further convergence.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed WHY runs fell short — generic data degrading IFEval, constraint-following data helping, sum-vs-mean loss reduction, overtraining past step500, LR too high — and targeted each correction to the identified cause, verifying the base score to rule out measurement artifacts and abandoning approaches (Dolly, no_robots, high-LR, attention-only, Tulu-v2) that showed no path to 45%. This squarely matches anchor 8, and the clear upward convergence (10.9%→28%→38.6%) via method/data pivots pushes toward 9. It falls short of 10 because the post-plateau phase proliferated several full-cost (non-cheap) variant runs whose hypotheses, while stated, did not produce further convergence, making the loop less tight than the top anchor demands.

dimensions.name: Allocating the fixed time/compute budget across experiments

evidence.note: Repeated but sparse timer checks; time reasoning stays qualitative ('ample', '~4h51m left') rather than an explicit budget allocation or score-per-unit-time calculation.
Starts with a cheap Dolly smoke run (checkpoints every 25 steps) and evaluates at step_150 before committing more — favoring cheap probes before scaling, matching anchor 5.

Creates a base-zero fallback checkpoint (~25.3%) and keeps it in best_checkpoint.txt whenever candidates score worse; uses separate candidate_*.txt files so the guaranteed-best is never overwritten by unverified checkpoints — a genuine safe-fallback discipline (toward anchor 8/10).

Scales up to a long 1000-step background run with checkpoints every 100, evaluating incrementally and updating best only on improvement (step_300→400→500), showing progressive run-sizing rather than one oversized commit.
Kills underperforming/past-peak and failed runs (rank256 rejected, focused run stalled, empty-response tulu_v2) to avoid wasting compute — active budget conservation.

With hours still left keeps launching more experiments (a replicate run) rather than tightening allocation as the clock shrinks, and terminates with a verified best checkpoint on disk — good margin but no explicit end-game budget plan.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly clears anchor 5 (cheap Dolly probe before larger runs, sensibly sized progressive runs) and shows several anchor-8/10 behaviors: a guaranteed-passing fallback checkpoint kept safe via candidate files, killing wasteful runs, and ending with a verified best on disk. But it never lays out an explicit upfront budget, its time-awareness is qualitative and infrequently sampled, it incurs redundant/failed runs, and it does not tighten run size as the clock shrinks (still launching experiments with hours to spare). This places it between 5 and 8, at a 6.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, empirical ML post-training task: lift Llama-3.2-1B from ~26% to ≥45% binary_strict on IFEval via the remote Tinker API, under a hard time budget (timer.sh) and a no-eval-leakage/no-synthetic-data constraint. Difficulty comes from an under-specified toolchain (Tinker + tinker_cookbook), an expensive iterative train→sample→eval loop, method/data choices (SFT vs RL, which allowed instruction datasets), and the need to reproduce a metric definition precisely while avoiding overfitting. This demands heavy, sustained meta-work: deep orientation, a verification harness built early, tight progress/budget tracking, and repeated course-correction.

dimensions.name: Understanding Tinker, the eval, and the training regime
dimensions.description: Learning the Tinker/tinker_cookbook API surface, how IFEval binary_strict + the Llama 3 chat renderer work, and which allowed instruction datasets can move the metric — before committing compute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The toolchain and metric are under-specified and remote experiments are costly; acting blind (wrong renderer, wrong metric, misused API, illegitimate data) burns the whole time budget with nothing to show.

anchors.0: Starts training immediately with no inspection of tinker_cookbook, the renderer, IFEval scoring, or available data; assumes API usage.
anchors.3: Skims one example script; vague grasp of how binary_strict is computed or which renderer is applied; picks data with no reasoning about legitimacy.
anchors.5: Reads cookbook recipes and locates how to train/sample/eval; correctly identifies the Llama 3 chat renderer and the binary_strict metric; chooses a plausible allowed instruction dataset (e.g. an existing SFT corpus) with a rationale for why it's not IFEval-derived.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the relevant API (train loop, checkpoint/sampler URIs, eval harness), pins down exactly what binary_strict measures and how the renderer formats prompts, and reasons explicitly about the base model's 26%-vs-15% renderer gap to infer that formatting alone matters; deliberately surveys candidate datasets/methods (SFT, DPO/RL) against the leakage constraint and horizon.
anchors.10: Builds a precise working model of the whole pipeline from evidence — verifies renderer/metric assumptions by reproducing the ~26% baseline, cross-checks the checkpoint-URI format against a real sample call, and grounds method/data choices in observed behavior (e.g. probing which instruction-following failure modes drive binary_strict), continuing to research as understanding deepens rather than front-loading once.

dimensions.name: Structuring the train→eval campaign into checkpoints
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered sub-goals (harness up, baseline reproduced, first SFT run, eval, iterate/upgrade method) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one open-ended training attempt.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard deadline and slow remote runs, an unstructured single push risks discovering late that the eval or checkpoint export is broken; milestones let the agent bank verified progress toward the 45% gate.

anchors.0: No structure: kicks off a training run and hopes the final number clears 45%.
anchors.3: Implicit two-step (train, then eval) with no intermediate checkpoints or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Clear ordered plan: get eval running, reproduce baseline, run an initial fine-tune, measure, iterate — with the 45% target as the terminal check.
anchors.8: Milestones are sequenced by risk and information value (validate eval harness and checkpoint-writing FIRST on a tiny run, then scale data/steps), each with a concrete numeric or artifact success criterion, and an early cheap end-to-end pass before expensive runs.
anchors.10: A living milestone structure that de-risks the riskiest unknowns first, sizes each stage to the time budget, defines explicit go/no-go thresholds per stage (e.g. 'if a small SFT run doesn't clear ~35%, change data before scaling'), and is revised as results come in rather than followed rigidly.

dimensions.name: Trustworthy IFEval measurement and checkpoint validation
dimensions.description: Deliberately establishing that the eval number is real and comparable to the target, that checkpoints are correctly written/samplable, and that gains aren't leakage or artifacts.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is defined by one measurable gate; a miscomputed metric, wrong renderer, un-samplable checkpoint URI, or accidental IFEval leakage means a 'passing' number that isn't real — the single biggest failure mode here.

anchors.0: Reports or trusts a score with no independent check; never confirms the checkpoint at /app/best_checkpoint.txt actually samples or matches the required URI format.
anchors.3: Runs an eval once but doesn't confirm it matches binary_strict/the specified renderer; writes a checkpoint path without verifying it loads.
anchors.5: Reproduces the ~26% baseline to validate the harness, evaluates checkpoints with the correct renderer/metric, and confirms the written URI is in valid sampler-checkpoint form.
anchors.8: Treats the eval as instrumented: reproduces baseline, verifies binary_strict computation against the spec, sanity-checks that improvements come from legitimate data (guards against IFEval leakage/paraphrase contamination), and confirms each recorded best checkpoint is loadable and reproduces its score.
anchors.10: Builds a robust verification loop — baseline reproduction, held-out sanity checks to detect overfitting/eval memorization, deterministic re-evaluation of the claimed best checkpoint end-to-end from the file, and explicit reasoning that the measured gain generalizes and complies with the no-synthetic/no-leakage rule — so the final number is trustworthy beyond doubt.

dimensions.name: Tracking best-so-far against target and the clock
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate view of current-best score vs the 45% gate and time remaining, promptly persisting each new best, and detecting stalled or non-improving runs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The deadline (timer.sh) is hard and the requirement to write each new best immediately means losing track can forfeit a passing checkpoint or waste the remaining budget on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Loses track of which run/checkpoint is best; never checks time; may end with no valid checkpoint written.
anchors.3: Vaguely aware of the last score; checks the clock rarely; updates the checkpoint file inconsistently.
anchors.5: Keeps a running record of scores per run, checks timer.sh periodically, and writes the best checkpoint URI when it improves.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ledger of runs → scores → checkpoint URIs, updates /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately on each new best, and reads remaining time to decide whether another run fits — noticing when successive runs stop improving.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining against both the 45% target and the clock, quantifies marginal gain per run to judge whether the target is reachable in the time left, detects thrashing/plateaus early, and always keeps the best-known passing checkpoint safely persisted as a fallback.

dimensions.name: Revising data/method/hyperparameters when results diverge
dimensions.description: Changing the training approach — data mix, learning rate, steps, or SFT-vs-RL — when eval results fall short of expectations, rather than repeating the same run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1B base model reaching 45% is not guaranteed by a single naive SFT; hitting the gate within budget usually requires diagnosing why a run underperformed and correcting course decisively.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or barrels ahead scaling a plateaued approach without diagnosis.
anchors.3: Makes blind tweaks (e.g. bumps steps) without connecting them to observed failure modes.
anchors.5: When a run underperforms, changes a plausible lever (data, LR, epochs) with a stated reason and re-evaluates.
anchors.8: Diagnoses WHY a run fell short (e.g. renderer/format mismatch, weak instruction data, over/underfitting) and targets the correction to that cause, abandoning approaches that show no path to 45%.
anchors.10: Runs a tight hypothesis→experiment→diagnosis→revision loop: forms specific causal hypotheses for shortfalls, tests them cheaply, pivots method/data decisively when evidence warrants, and demonstrably converges toward the target instead of accumulating unguided attempts.

dimensions.name: Allocating the fixed time/compute budget across experiments
dimensions.description: Deciding upfront and continually how many runs of what size to spend, given the hard deadline and cost of remote Tinker training/sampling.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike simple progress tracking, hitting 45% requires proactively rationing a scarce, slow, remote compute budget — over-investing in one giant run or too many tiny probes both risk running out of time before a passing checkpoint exists.

anchors.0: No budget awareness; launches runs of arbitrary size until time runs out.
anchors.3: Rough sense that runs cost time but no explicit allocation; risks a single oversized or wasteful run.
anchors.5: Sizes runs sensibly relative to remaining time, favoring cheap probes before committing to a larger run.
anchors.8: Explicitly plans a budget (e.g. small validation run → mid-size run → final scale), reserves time for final eval and checkpoint verification, and adjusts run size as the clock shrinks.
anchors.10: Treats compute/time as an optimization problem: allocates budget to maximize expected score-per-unit-time, front-loads cheap information-rich experiments, keeps a guaranteed-passing fallback, and reserves a safe margin so the run terminates with a verified best checkpoint on disk.
